name: Giant Yang Na of Ban Nok, Ko Pha Ngan

location.address: Roadside, Ban Nok (Moo 2), Ban Tai subdistrict, Ko Pha Ngan, Surat Thani, about 300 m past Wat Pho

access: Free, beside the public road, open at all hours; daytime advised. Narrow road, busy about 11:00 to 14:00. Few facilities. Villagers treat it as sacred; small shrines at the foot.
transport: About 4 to 5 km from Thong Sala pier; Thong Sala to Ban Tai/Ban Khai songthaew, or taxi or hired motorbike (lovethailand, travellingfoot). Not checked on site.
verify_notes: Register: 400 years, girth 14.64 m, height 53.5 m (girth measured by the register, presumably at breast height; may include buttress swell, unverified). Many more Yang Na stand in the same area, this being the 'mother tree'. Bees nest in the crown. Cared for by the Ban Nok community (Moo 2). story:
On a narrow road through Ban Nok, a village in the south of Ko Pha Ngan, one Yang Na rises as a pale grey column past the power lines and only starts to branch far above the rooftops.

Thailand's Ministry of Culture listed it in 2018 as a heritage tree of the land and recorded a girth of 14.64 metres, a height of 53.5 metres and an age of about 400 years. The age is an estimate, so read it as a rough figure. The register adds that the tree won first prize in a 1999 Kasetsart University contest for the largest Yang Na and calls it the biggest in Thailand. That is the register's claim, and we have not found a national survey to check it against.

Yang Na is a tall tropical tree of the dipterocarp family, and more of them grow around the village. The register notes that bees nest in this one's crown. Ban Nok treats the tree as sacred, with small spirit houses at its foot, coloured cloth wound round the trunk and a low wooden fence keeping the ground clear.

It stands beside the public road about 300 metres past Wat Pho, a few kilometres from the Thong Sala pier, and is free to see at any hour. Come in daylight, because the road is narrow. If you go, tell us how it looks now.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its pale grey trunk, bare for most of its height, rising from a fenced plot beside the road with small spirit houses and coloured cloth at its foot, about 300 metres past Wat Pho in Ban Nok.
